body:
Problem:
On Windows, `vim.ui.open()` passes URLs to `cmd.exe /c start`. cmd.exe treats `&` as a command separator, so a URL such as `https://example.com/?q=hello&t=brave` opens as `https://example.com/?q=hello`.

Solution:
Caret-escape `&|<>^` in URIs when the open handler is `cmd.exe`.

Fixes #41337

+• |vim.ui.open()| on Windows no longer truncates URLs at `&`.

@@ -199,6 +199,9 @@ function M.open(path, opt)
     if open_cmd[1] == 'xdg-open' then
       job_opt.stdout = false
       job_opt.stderr = false
+    elseif open_cmd[1] == 'cmd.exe' and is_uri then
+      -- cmd.exe /c treats "&", "|", "<", ">" as metacharacters. #41337
+      path = path:gsub('([&|<>^])', '^%1')

comment_regular_data.body:
`cmd.exe` also might expand `%VAR%`, if there is valid var name between two `%`
Shouldn't be problem for typical encoded urls like `.../hello%20world`

Did some new llm testing for benchmarking and it suggested:
```lua 
return { 'rundll32', 'url.dll,FileProtocolHandler' }, nil
``` 
for urls from `M._get_open_cmd`, though it looks bare and might be too much

> it suggested:
> 
> ```lua
> return { 'rundll32', 'url.dll,FileProtocolHandler' }, nil
> ```

see previous PRs/issues for discussion of that, and why we moved to cmd.exe. I'm not saying we shouldn't do that, I'm saying refer to those discussions to see the tradeoffs.

> `cmd.exe` also might expand `%VAR%`

should we escape "%" here too?

> > `cmd.exe` also might expand `%VAR%`
> 
> should we escape "%" here too?

Yes: `path = path:gsub('([&|<>^%%])', '^%1')`

But there is tricky edge case if user got [`delayed expansion`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/cmd#:~:text=environment%20variable%20expansion.-,/v%3Aoff,-Disables%20delayed%20environment) enabled. **(disabled by default on windows)**

`cmd.exe` supports two environment-variable syntaxes:

```cmd
%PATH%     rem normal expansion
!PATH!     rem delayed expansion
```

so might as well handle `https://example.com/?q=!NAME!`, and it seems can't simply escape it cause the expansion happens later (well it's named delayed after all)

`return { 'cmd.exe', '/d', '/v:off', '/c', 'start', '' }, nil` - if `is_uri `+ windows we might as well do this

_better to reconfirm Im a bit busy rn though_

> so might as well handle `https://example.com/?q=!NAME!`

sure. adding `^` should be harmless anyway.
